translationRepairs: Precious Origin 2, when the heir was born, he returned to the Pu mansion.
Precious Origin 2, when Prince Yu was born, he returned to the Pu mansion.
Source 豫王生 names Prince Yu’s birth, not an unnamed heir; “the heir” invents heirship absent from the Chinese, and “Prince Yu” restores the titled person.
In the second year of Precious Origin, when the Heir Apparent was born, he returned to the Pu residence.
In the second year of Precious Origin, when Prince Yu was born, he returned to the Pu residence.
豫王 is the titled Prince Yu; “Heir Apparent” (太子) is not in the Chinese, so rendering him as Heir Apparent is a factual mistranslation.
Third month, renyin: the tomb of Prince Zhao was restored and staffed with guardians.
Third month, renyin: the tomb of the Qin Mourning Prince was restored and staffed with guardians.
秦悼王 is the Qin Mourning Prince (fief Qin + posthumous 悼); “Prince Zhao” drops 秦 and misreads 悼, so the proposed title is the accurate fix.
Western tribesman Zha Qimizheng of the Zhaizi came in.
Zha Qimizheng, son of the western tribesman Zha Zhan, came in to submit.
瞎氊子瞎欺米征 is kinship plus personal name—son of 瞎氊 named 瞎欺米征—and 內附 means submission; “Zhaizi” invents a tribe and omits the father–son link.
